findings.suggested_investigation: Locate the definitions of KpLog_SetFallbackFile and KpLog_SetFallbackLevel (KpLog.h / KpLog.cpp in Common or _shared_src, a cited callee). Check whether they only assign a static char buffer or a POD and whether any global they touch has a non-trivial constructor. If so, move the call into the KPatchInit / registration path, which runs after static init.
findings.why_it_matters: A namespace-scope initializer that calls into the logging library runs in static-init order, so it can run before the logger's own statics (fallback file/level storage, critical sections, the kpatch log handle) are constructed. If KpLog_SetFallbackFile touches any such state, or allocates a std::string, the result is undefined and can fail only at load time. The `g_fallbackSet` value is also never read, so the side effect is the only purpose.
